annotations.text: Consisted of hearing loss per 25 dB and age. Hearing loss was defined by the average of hearing thresholds (0.5-4 kHz) in the better hearing ear. Age was adjusted for as a categorical variable (70-74, 75-79, ≥80 years). The National Health and Nutrition Examination Surveys report individuals aged 80 years or older as 80 years to ensure participant confidentiality.
Demographic factors include sex, race, level of education, and annual household income.

Cardiovascular risk factors include hypertension, stroke, diabetes mellitus, and cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, angina, congestive heart failure), smoking history (current, former, never).

Number of individuals included in each model. Individuals with missing data for a given model were excluded from that model. For analyses of hospitalization, missing data comprised less than 1.1% of the data set, and for burden of disease, missing data comprised less than 7.1% of the data set.
The OR represents the odds of the next higher categorical number of hospitalizations.
Abbreviation: OR, odds ratio. Estimates are per 25 dB greater hearing threshold in the better-hearing ear. All models use survey sample weights and the complex NHANES design.

Source wording conflict: the table title refers generally to the previous 12 months, but the disease-burden block explicitly specifies >10 days in the past 30 days, agreeing with Methods. The 30-day period is retained for these outcomes.

tables.notes: All 5 source data rows and all 3 model specifications are exported. Each OR and its 95% CI remain together in one source-display CSV cell, including the line break and footnote e where printed. The domain column carries the source row-block labels.

result_groups.title: Hearing acuity, hospitalization, and self-reported health in older US adults
result_groups.question: How is hearing acuity associated with hospitalization and self-reported disease burden among adults aged 70 years or older?
result_groups.investigation: One cross-sectional analysis of pooled 2005-2006 and 2009-2010 NHANES participants with audiometric testing.
result_groups.grouping_reason: All local results concern this single identified observational investigation. Different health outcomes and nested adjustment models remain within the same substantive question. Demographic and unweighted outcome comparisons characterize the same cohort and its potential confounders. The main adjusted estimates are designated below; shared source tables do not supply the family boundary.
result_groups.summary: Worse hearing was associated with hospitalization and >10 days of poor physical or mental health after adjustment. No statistically significant fully adjusted association was reported for health-related inactivity. Cross-sectional data do not establish temporal ordering or causation.

source_snippets.text:
Consisted of hearing loss per 25 dB and age. Hearing loss was defined by the average of hearing thresholds (0.5-4 kHz) in the better hearing ear. Age was adjusted for as a categorical variable (70-74, 75-79, ≥80 years). The National Health and Nutrition Examination Surveys report individuals aged 80 years or older as 80 years to ensure participant confidentiality.
Demographic factors include sex, race, level of education, and annual household income.
Cardiovascular risk factors include hypertension, stroke, diabetes mellitus, and cardiovascular disease (myocardial infarction, coronary artery disease, angina, congestive heart failure), smoking history (current, former, never).
